items.title: 🔓 [Country Life] Architects and ancestry: The country house that's spent 900 years in the same family
items.content_html: Steven Brindle looks at the remarkable history of Burton Constable Hall, in the East Riding of Yorkshire —of a house that has never been sold, but has descended for nine centuries as an inheritance. Photographs by Paul Highnam for Country Life.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Wangshan Qingshui Water Treatment Plant / POA Architects
items.content_html: Wangshan Qingshui Water Treatment Plant stands in Qianku, Cangnan County, Wenzhou, where housing, cultivated land and river channels meet. With architectural scheme design by POA Architects, the facility brings treatment basins, production buildings and connecting spaces into a legible above-ground ensemble.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Minthis Resort Development / Woods Bagot
items.content_html: Minthis is a resort-style development located in the hillside setting of Tsada Village in Paphos. With Cypriot developer Pafilia, Woods Bagot's London studio delivered master planning, architecture, interior design, and branding services to create a unique retreat-style experience, combining the best of local antiquity and premium amenities.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Maryland House / Remi C.T.
items.content_html: A bold example of infill housing architecture, Maryland House redefines urban living through spatial innovation and design precision. It is a dwelling that challenges traditional spatial hierarchy in the home to focus on the reality of modern city living.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Vandeuren III-IV / P&P Architectes + Atelier d'Architecture A4
items.content_html: Winner of the Be-Exemplary Award 2019, Vandeuren III and IV is part of an ambitious renovation strategy for social housing in Brussels. The project transforms 160 dwellings into 132 reconfigured units while integrating shared facilities and a reorganization of outdoor spaces. The intervention combines heritage preservation, quality of use, and circularity, enhancing the existing fabric while responding to contemporary needs.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Minou-On Apartment Renovation / CROSSARCHITECTURE / Mehrdad Makaremi
items.content_html: In Minou-On Apartment, a thirty-year-old duplex in Tehran gains a villa-like quality as a former terrace becomes a skylit, planted void. A timber system connects the home's two floors, working with the exposed concrete frame to reorganize rooms, circulation, and everyday life.

items.title: 🔓 [Popular Mechanics] Our Cities Are Shrinking. Does That Mean They’re Doomed to Be Unlivable?
items.content_html: Population decline could leave thousands of cities struggling to maintain aging pipes, roads, and buildings. An engineer says it’s not too late to make the choices that will revive urban life.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Argyle House: The Story Behind Edinburgh’s Brutalist Landmark
items.content_html: Rising from the rocks that form the base of Castle Rock in Edinburgh, Argyle House stands in stark contrast to the city's most iconic landmark. Built in the late 1960s, this angular, grey building is a quintessential example of post-war Brutalist architecture. A geometric concrete structure stripped of ornamentation that has recently become an unlikely star on screen, serving as the backdrop for the series Dept. Q, based on novels by Danish author Jussi Adler-Olsen. Yet the 11-story complex, which once housed government offices and now homes promising startups, continues to divide opinion. On one hand, its imposing presence challenges the historic urban fabric; on the other, its architectural significance makes it an important part of the city's modern heritage.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Mekong Breeze House / Re: Edge Architecture
items.content_html: Mekong Breeze House celebrates Cambodia's tropical spirit — where sunlight dances through patterned terracotta screens, and the river breeze flows freely under and through operable windows, sliding panels, and open spaces. Designed in harmony with nature, its U-shaped formation embraces the landscape and the view of the Mekong, preserving existing trees and creating a living sanctuary of comfort, culture, and calm.

items.title: [ArchDaily] BALSA (Self-Sufficient Boat for Laboratories and Services in the Amazon) / CASA [Ciudades Auto Sostenibles Amazónicas]
items.content_html: Amazonian living is characterized by the geographical dispersion of its communities and high territorial mobility. In the Peruvian low jungle, river transport is the main connection between riverside populations, but long travel times and high costs make accessing basic services difficult. Furthermore, the small size of many communities limits the state's capacity to provide permanent infrastructure for healthcare, education, identity registration, and other essential services. Consequently, the Amazon region concentrates some of the lowest indicators in the country regarding access to education, healthcare services, and development opportunities.

items.title: [Canadian Architect] A Seat at the Table: BEACAP Celebrates One Year of Building Equality in Architecture
items.content_html: What does a more equitable architecture profession look like? In Ottawa–Gatineau, a growing community of architects, designers, and advocates is working to answer that question—and turn the conversation into action. This fall marks one year since Building Equality in Architecture Capital Region (BEACAP) joined the national Building Equality in Architecture (BEA) network, becoming its eighth…

items.title: [ArchDaily] House in the Woods / Tom Lontine Architect
items.content_html: Set within a sloped, wooded site overlooking the Connecticut River, House in the Woods by Tom Lontine Architect is a 4,400-square-foot residence designed for a pair of hardworking professionals seeking a quiet home to age in place. Low-slung and clad in dark-stained cedar, the house is embedded into the hillside to minimize its visual impact and heighten the sense of immersion in the surrounding forest.

items.title: [ArchDaily] What to Consider When Integrating Photovoltaics into Building Facades
items.content_html: When considering building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV), the potential is clear: making the building envelope an active part of a building's energy strategy. Yet specifying these systems can be difficult when the process is unfamiliar. How much electricity can a facade generate? What will the system cost? Which orientations and areas are suitable? And how should the photovoltaic panels be integrated with the building's structural, electrical, and fire-safety requirements? Without clear answers, assessing feasibility, establishing budgets, and involving consultants and contractors can become difficult.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Comporta House / Aurora Arquitectos
items.content_html: The house is located in the village of Carvalhal, on the Alentejo coast in southern Portugal. Here, long sandy beaches extend inland into flat pine-forested terrain. Those who come here to live or vacation are seeking silence.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Freedom Mobile Arch Amphitheatre / Revery Architecture
items.content_html: Framing views of Vancouver's North Shore Mountains, the Freedom Mobile Arch is an open-air amphitheatre designed to remain connected to its surrounding landscape. A sweeping mass-timber canopy shelters audiences of up to 10,000 while preserving the experience of being outdoors. Permanent infrastructure and adaptable seating allow the venue to accommodate performances and gatherings at a wide range of scales.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Danubio Budapest Building / T2.a Architects
items.content_html: Designed by T2a Architects and completed recently on the site of a former river gravel pit on the banks of the Danube in Budapest, the Danubio residential building responds to the unique urban and natural environment, partially overriding the rules of Budapest real estate developers, and realizes a concept that treats sustainability not only as a slogan but also revives many pre-existing but now forgotten architectural solutions and recreates them in a modern, timeless form.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Planá Kindergarten  / PROAM ARCHITEKTI
items.content_html: The new municipal kindergarten in Planá, South Bohemia, represents a sensitive yet confident introduction of modern architecture into a historic rural setting. A sustainable public building made of timber has been created on a small but visually prominent site. Its form immediately reveals its purpose—a building for children that is part traditional, part modern, and somewhat fairytale-like.
